name: Patriot
blurb: The Army's workhorse interceptor against aircraft, cruise missiles and ballistic missiles. Eighteen other countries use it, so the U.S. competes with allies, Ukraine included, for every missile off the line.

deliveriesPerYear.note: Table 2: five-year average of U.S. procurement.

announcedCapacityPerYear.quote: The surge annual production rate with existing tooling and facilities is 2,000.
announcedCapacityPerYear.note: All customers. About half of current output goes to allies and partners.

fy27Request.quote: the 3,203 Patriot missiles requested in the Army’s FY 2027 budget

fy27DeliveriesBegin.quote: These are projected to start delivery in May 2029.

lotMonths.note: Table 2: production time for a full lot.

rebuildOutlook.quote: heavily used in this war—will take three or more years from today to return to prewar inventory levels.

name: THAAD
fullName: Terminal High Altitude Area Defense interceptor
blurb: Hits ballistic missiles higher and farther out than Patriot. CSIS calls it the most critical of the seven because stocks are small and nothing else does its job.

deliveriesPerYear.note: Table 2: five-year average of U.S. procurement.

announcedCapacityPerYear.quote: Lockheed Martin plans to expand production capacity to 400 a year
announcedCapacityPerYear.note: All customers; current surge rate is 96 a year.

fy27Request.quote: The Army has requested 857 THAAD interceptors in FY 2027.

fy27DeliveriesBegin.quote: Their deliveries, projected to start in mid-2029

lotMonths.note: Table 2: production time for a full lot.

rebuildOutlook.quote: will complete the replacement of Iran War usage by the end of calendar year 2029.

name: SM-3
blurb: Ship-launched interceptor that hits ballistic missiles in space. At about $29M each it's the most expensive missile here, and the slowest to build.

deliveriesPerYear.note: Table 2: 40/yr Block IB plus 13/yr Block IIA ("SM-3 IIA 13 57 7 64").

fy27Request.quote: 78 SM-3 Block IBs, 136 SM-3 Block IIAs, and 540 SM-6s

fy27DeliveriesBegin.quote: These orders will take between 36 and 39 months to begin deliveries once Congress provides appropriations.
fy27DeliveriesBegin.note: Assumes appropriations in October 2026, plus 37 months.

lotMonths.note: Table 2: production time for a full Block IB lot.

rebuildOutlook.quote: inventories will not return to prewar levels until early 2029 despite the relatively low usage in the campaign.

name: SM-6

name: Tomahawk
blurb: Long-range cruise missile fired from ships and submarines at targets on land. Used in every major U.S. campaign since 1991.

deliveriesPerYear.note: Table 2: five-year average of U.S. procurement.

announcedCapacityPerYear.quote: RTX announced it will increase annual TLAM production to more than 1,000 under the framework agreement

name: JASSM
blurb: A stealthy cruise missile dropped from aircraft out of range of enemy air defenses. B-52s flying from Britain launched them all the way to the ceasefire.

deliveriesPerYear.note: Table 2: five-year average of U.S. procurement. CSIS's May update says production is already at its surge rate.

lotMonths.note: Table 2: production time for a full lot.

rebuildOutlook.quote: Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile (JASSM) and Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) will take several months to a year to replace.

name: PrSM
blurb: The Army's new 500+ km ballistic missile, replacing ATACMS. Deliveries only began in 2023, so the stockpile was small going in.
